topic: The arbitrary-rank all-length minus-one-eighth pointer-product conjecture in Section 4 of Abbott et al., arXiv:1805.09364v3
title: Extending Sun–Luo–Ye bounds to refute Abbott et al.'s pointer-product conjecture

creators.name: Zhang, Wenlin
creators.affiliation: National University of Singapore; ChronoAI Pte Ltd, Singapore

abstract: Extending the spectral bounds of Sun, Luo and Ye [Mathematics of Operations Research 45, 233–271 (2020)], we refute the arbitrary-rank interpretation of the pointer-product conjecture of Abbott, Silva, Wechs, Brunner and Branciard [Quantum 3, 194 (2019), Section 4, p. 5, after equation (26); arXiv:1805.09364v3]. Three orthogonal projections on C^3 give the normalized weak-limit pointer product -1/6 < -1/8. For n measurements in unrestricted finite dimension, the exact minimum is -c_n, where c_1=0 and c_(n+1)=(1+c_n)^2/[8(1-c_n)]. Codimension-one projections attain every finite-length minimum, and c_n increases to 1/3. Thus pointer products have infimum -1/3, separated by 2/3 from the limiting ordered weak value -1. The same bounds hold as envelopes at every finite coupling strength for independent centered Gaussian pointers.
summary: An extension of Sun–Luo–Ye spectral bounds to sequential weak-pointer products: an exact three-projection counterexample, sharp finite-length minima with explicit attaining projections, the sharp uniform gap, and finite-strength Gaussian envelopes.
posing_locator: Section 4, printed page 5, paragraph after equation (26); nested-product definition in equation (A42), printed page 14

verification_scope.lean_statement: Negation of the universal -1/8 nested-product inequality using three rational projections on C^3 and state e_3; formal parameter n=2 represents three observables.
written_proofs: finite-strength centered Gaussian envelope and final-pointer independence
verification_scope.finite_checks: Exact rational and symbolic identities, exact three-dimensional extremizer, six Gaussian finite-coupling controls, eight attaining constructions through n=64, 360 seeded matrix controls and four sets of 144 sibling controls.
